setlist.title: Sitting On Top Of The World

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Me and My Uncle** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds this Me and My Uncle interesting and different from other versions they own; Hearing Jerry sing lead on Me and My Uncle is described as a special, unusual treat [9][13]
- **Doin' That Rag** (2 reviews): The transition from Doin' That Rag into High Time is described as seamless, serene and beautiful; Reviewer believes they hear pedal steel in the first half of Doin' That Rag, which the notes don't mention [7][15]
- **Slewfoot** (1 review): Jerry plays steel guitar on Slewfoot and Silver Threads and Golden Needles, opening the show in old-school fashion [10]
- **Mama Tried** (1 review): Played at a slower tempo than usual, and described as very early for the song [12]
- **High Time** (1 review): Reviewer calls this High Time (6:11) a top-class version, and considers Pigpen's work on the show his best [8]
- **Sitting On Top Of The World** (1 review): Jerry reportedly tears up the licks on Sitting On Top Of The World and Lovelight [13]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Lovelight closing the show is praised, alongside pedal steel on the country numbers [14]
- **I'm a King Bee** (1 review): Reviewer calls King Bee outstanding [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Slewfoot**: rare: 9 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd69-06-28.sbd.samaritano.20548.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 9 songs; 71 min; rated 4.42/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard version sounds good but has some audible background hiss on the ogg; not pristine, though very listenable; This version sounds overly bright, possibly from an undecoded Dolby B cassette; lowering the treble EQ helps, and the difference is slight [5][11]
- **gd69-06-28.sbd.cole.3300.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 70 min; rated 3.89/5 by 9 [2]
- **gd1969-06-28.166577.sbd.anon.gems.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 73 min [3]

## Around the show

- Pigpen raps and stretches his songs to full length during the show [10]
- Peter Grant plays banjo and Marmaduke sings backup vocals on Me and My Uncle [1]
- David Nelson plays guitar on Slewfoot and Mama Tried; Garcia plays pedal steel on Slewfoot and Silver Threads [3]
- Compared with the other circulating version, which sounds overly dull, this one is brighter [11]
- Unlike psychedelic-era shows, it opens with a countrified bluegrass string band sound, with no Dark Star, Other One or space [13]
- Show sits at a transitional point, moving from the psychedelic sound peaking at the Ark in Boston in April toward folk-country [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-06-28.sbd.samaritano.20548.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Joe Samaritano; source: Soundboard (no DAE) [1]. Also: The DAT seed was provided by Michael P. Weitzman [1]
- **gd69-06-28.sbd.cole.3300.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Brian Cole; source: Soundboard (DAE) [2]. Also: This is the complete show; Lovelight is missing on some earlier circulating copies [2]
- **gd1969-06-28.166577.sbd.anon.gems.flac16**: taped by Anon; transferred by Mastering by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: SBD master reel > DAT > AIF [3]. Also: Aired on KXCI Tucson's Dead Air with Jim Blackwood on December 24, 2023, then shared to shnflac.net the next day [3]
